title: THE LIFEBOAT TWO YARDS BUILT
deck: A surge is nine days off and the condemned ferry cannot sail. Two boatyards that have not shared a slip in thirty years each remember a drowning the other's boat would repeat; Illuminara asks them what the sea did first.
shape: Seven scenes across nine days: an argument on the shingle, a day in each yard, a chalk floor where one number turns out to be two and each master names what he would need to see, a night spent holding a hull still, a surveyor's gates and a trial in two seas with one family choosing to stay, and three crossings.

scenes.title: The Argument on the Shingle
paragraphs: *Skerrow, Tolland Slip · nine days before the surge, 06:40*

The ferry lay where the tide had left her, plating opened along one side like a tin. The surveyor's notice on her wheelhouse door was three days old. The forecast was newer: a surge in nine days, high water at 21:40, and a sea that would walk over the quay and into the lower village. Three hundred and ten people lived on Skerrow. The coastguard cutter could carry forty, if the sea allowed, and nobody would promise the sea.

Illuminara had come over on a fishing boat with a flask and a notebook. The council clerk had asked for hands that could hold a hull still while it was joined. Nobody had asked her for a design, and she was beginning to see why.
Two people had reached the slip from opposite ends of the shingle, and neither had slowed down.

**Magnus**  
There is a hull in my shed from the Orsay contract. Twenty-four metres, flat as a table, and she takes a bank like a hand takes a glove. I can have her on the slip by noon.

**Adaeze**  
And in the first following sea off the Sound she lies down. Flat doesn't grip. My brother learned that in the time it takes to say it. I won't send three hundred people out on a tray.

**Magnus**  
And your deep keel stands off Pellam Bank with nowhere to put its nose, and breaks up in the surf. My father learned that. Look at the stones.
Nobody looked at the stones. They looked at each other, the way people look at a wall they helped to build.

**Illuminara**  
I can hold a hull level while it is joined, and carry a load through it for a while. I can't draw a keel, and I can't draw a bank. Is each of you right about the other's boat?

**Adaeze**  
Yes.

**Magnus**  
Yes.

**Illuminara**  
Then I would like a day in each yard. Not to choose between you. To be corrected.
Magnus laughed first, short and unwilling. It was the first sound the two of them had made together in thirty years, and neither forgave the other for it.

scenes.title: The Loft
paragraphs: *Oyelaran yard, mould loft · nine days before the surge, 15:10*

Chalk lines covered the loft floor, every offset marked in Adaeze's fractions of a foot. A seventeen-year-old called Tobi had been told to teach the visitor to plane a keel timber and had decided to do it thoroughly.

**Tobi**  
Thumb forward. No, you're pushing the wood. The plane does the pushing. There. Hear that? That's a shaving, not a splinter.

Illuminara had stood inside a great many collapsing things and had never heard this sound. The oak smelled like a held breath. *I am being taught by a boy with sawdust in his eyebrows,* she thought, *and I am happier than I have been all week.*
Adaeze came up the stairs with two mugs and did not sit.

**Adaeze**  
Kehinde's boat was flat. A good boat, fast. Running home with the sea behind her, the stern came up on a wave and the bow dug, and for half a second she had nothing under her to hold the water. Then she swung beam-on, and the next wave finished it.

**Illuminara**  
What did the sea do first?

**Adaeze**  
The stern lifted. Everyone asks how big the wave was. You're the first to ask what it did first.
Illuminara wrote *stern lifts, no grip, swings beam-on* in her notebook, and under it, *open water, sea behind.* Adaeze watched her write it the way one watches a stranger handle a tool one has made.

**Adaeze**  
A keel is not a theory. It's the part of the boat that remembers the water.

scenes.title: The Bank
paragraphs: *Fenn yard, ramp and shingle · eight days before the surge, 07:20*

Wick, sixteen, put a chain in her hands and moved her grip before she had closed them. Everything on the Fenn ramp was measured in the yard's own rule, tenths of a foot, in pencil on the planking. Magnus walked the shingle beside her and told it to the stones rather than to her.

**Magnus**  
My father's boat had a good deep keel. Fine in the Sound. At Harbour Tarn there was no quay, only a bank like Pellam. He brought her in to ground her, and the keel took the shingle and stopped her dead while the surf kept coming. She lay down forty yards from dry stones.

**Illuminara**  
What did the sea do first?
He looked at her as if she had been impertinent. Then he answered.

**Magnus**  
The keel stopped. First. Then she turned over.

That night, on a sheet of the yard's brown paper, Illuminara wrote the two answers side by side. Adaeze's brother had died in open water, with the sea behind him and nothing to grip. Magnus's father had died on a bank, with the sea on the beam and too much to grip. *Two boats,* she thought. *Two different minutes of the same crossing.* Nobody had ever asked one hull to survive both.

scenes.title: Seven in Two Languages
paragraphs: *The old sail loft · seven days before the surge, 21:30*

Lamplight, and the two masters on opposite sides of it. Tobi and Wick stood against the wall with the look of apprentices who expect to be sent out. Illuminara had chalked two columns on the floor, every figure converted into millimetres. In one: OPEN WATER, SEA BEHIND. Needs grip along the length. In the other: THE BANK. Needs a flat bottom and nothing that can dig.

On the table lay a third sheet, brown at the folds, found at the bottom of the island's drawing chest. The Marigold, the one boat the two yards had ever drawn together, thirty years ago. Her keel was drawn at seven.

**Illuminara**  
Both your hands are on this sheet. What does seven mean?

**Adaeze**  
Seven-eighths of a foot.

**Magnus**  
Seven-tenths. It's what seven has always meant.

Seven-eighths of a foot is two hundred and sixty-seven millimetres. Seven-tenths is two hundred and thirteen. The Marigold had been built fifty-four millimetres too shallow, and she had rolled on her moorings the night she was launched, and for thirty years each yard had known exactly whose fault that was.
Nobody said sorry. Adaeze took the chalk and wrote 267 beside the seven. Magnus, after a long moment, took it from her and wrote 213 beneath it, and the two of them stood looking at the difference.

**Illuminara**  
Both are good drawings. You were reading one number in two languages.

**Magnus**  
Then show me a boat that does both, and I'll stop saying it can't be built.

**Adaeze**  
A board through the bottom. Down in the Sound, with the sea behind her, it gives her something to hold.

**Magnus**  
A hole in the bottom of a boat. That is near enough how my father went.

**Adaeze**  
The hole stays where it is, below the water. What changes is a case round it, welded up to the deck, so the sea rises inside the case to the level outside and no higher. The lid sits above her loaded waterline.

**Magnus**  
A case cracks. Then it's a hole with a lid on.

**Adaeze**  
Then it is filled with water and watched all night before she moves. And hear what the board is. It is grip along her length and nothing else. It does not steer her and it is not ballast. She still wants her rudder, her weight in the right place and someone on the helm who knows a following sea.

**Magnus**  
And on the bank the board is down and she stops dead, the way he did.

**Tobi**  
Raise it before she lands. And if she meets shingle with the board half down it should kick up, not dig. A pin that shears. A winch to haul it, and a crank for when the winch won't.
Nobody answered an apprentice for a while. Adaeze looked at Magnus. Magnus looked at Wick, who looked at the floor, and then, with some effort, at Tobi.

**Illuminara**  
I can't tell you whether it will work. I can ask what each of you would have to see before the other's hand is on your work.

**Adaeze**  
In a two-and-a-half-metre sea from astern, board down, she holds her heading within fifteen degrees for five waves running. Measured with the surveyor's compass, not remembered. Otherwise Kehinde's boat sails again with my name on it.

**Magnus**  
Nothing under her bottom when she touches shingle. The board housed by pin or by crank inside twenty seconds, and I watch her take the bank twice, once slow and once not. Otherwise it's my father's boat under three hundred people.
Then each of them did the thing the other had been waiting thirty years for, and attacked the drawing instead of the man.

**Magnus**  
Your board is drawn for the deep Sound. A hundred and fifty millimetres off its depth, and the pin shears at a load I can watch it shear at.

**Adaeze**  
A hundred and fifty is grip I would rather keep.

**Magnus**  
Then it digs.

**Adaeze**  
And your stern is cut square. A following sea sits on a square stern like a hand on a table. I want it faired before I trust the board to hold her.
Neither spoke for a time. The lamp ticked. Outside, the tide went out over the stones.

**Adaeze**  
Then the board is shorter. And you cut your Orsay hull.

**Magnus**  
Nobody has cut an Orsay hull. I'd cut it myself, in my own shed, and you check my frames in your units.

**Adaeze**  
And I fair the stern to your drawing, in your tenths.

On the brown sheet, under Tobi's pin, Adaeze wrote Magnus's condition and signed it, and Magnus wrote hers and signed it, each figure in feet or tenths and again in millimetres. Neither of them looked up while they did it.

**Magnus**  
Who owns what?

**Adaeze**  
Board, case and pivot are mine. Hull, ramp and the framing around the slot are yours.

**Magnus**  
I check your pivot load in your units.

**Adaeze**  
And I check your frames in yours. Then we both do it again in millimetres and sign each other's sheets.

**Illuminara**  
I'll hold her still while you cut.

scenes.title: Standing Still
paragraphs: *Tolland Slip, shed two · four days before the surge, 02:10*

Three days had gone into the hull, in the order Hanne Voss's sheet laid down. On the first, the Fenn yard stripped the deck and brought the Orsay hull to the slip. On the second, Oyelaran's plate shop rolled the case and the two yards framed round the slot line in alternating shifts, so that neither slept while the other's hands were on the boat. On the third, Hanne walked every frame with a torch, rejected two welds, and passed the rest at midnight and not before. Only then was the bottom to be cut.
She sat on her blocks now with a seam of lamplight where the slot would go. Fourteen tonnes of plating wanted to spring the moment Tobi's saw finished the first cut; a flat hull opens badly.

Illuminara laid both palms against the plating beside the line and took the load through herself, down her arms and her spine into the slip, the way one holds a door against wind. The plating stayed true. For fifty minutes Magnus cut and Tobi cut and Adaeze measured, and she did not move.

It cost her. Her hands shook long before the slot was done, and when Magnus said, without looking up, that she might let go, she sat down on an upturned bucket and could not lift a mug. Tobi brought her tea and, with a straight face, a plane.

**Tobi**  
Your grip is still wrong.
*Good,* she thought, and was surprised again by how much she meant it.

scenes.title: Two Seas
paragraphs: *Skerrow hill, Pellam Bank and Skerrow Sound · two days before the surge, 06:00*

Ruth Calloway's family did not come to the slip. Illuminara went up the hill instead and found Ruth on her step with a flask. Five of them lived in that house, and the church where her mother lay was thirty-four metres above the sea.

**Ruth**  
I've lived through eleven forecasts. We are staying.

**Illuminara**  
What would make staying less of a wager?

**Ruth**  
A radio that works. And somebody who comes for us if I'm wrong.

**Illuminara**  
I'll take that to the surveyor. If she can't make it hold, I'll come back and tell you so.

Between the cut and the water there had been two days. The case was welded, filled to the lid and watched through a night, and it held. The hoist and the crank were fitted. On the slip, Tobi's pin sheared under the rig at the load he had set, and sheared at the same load the second time. She went down the slip at first light, ugly, with the trunk running down her middle like a spine.
Hanne Voss was sixty and had refused certificates for far prettier boats. She read her conditions aloud before anyone touched the engine.

**Hanne**  
Abort thresholds first. Heel past fifteen degrees and holding, I call her in. A board that doesn't answer a command inside twenty seconds, I call her in. Water at the trunk lid, I call her in. Sea above three metres significant, I call her in. I will not be argued with, by either yard or by you.

She went through the boat before the bank, and she let both masters watch her do it. She put a torch down the trunk, ran a hand along the seams of the case, tried the pivot for play, read the freeboard against the ballast, and worked the hoist and then the crank herself, with a watch in her other hand. Seventeen seconds on the crank. She wrote it down.

At Pellam Bank, on the rising tide, the boat went at the shingle at two knots with the board housed. Her flat bottom rode up the bank and stopped without a shudder. Then, on Hanne's order, again at two knots with the board dropped halfway. It struck, the pin sheared, and the board swung up into its trunk like a hand taken off a hot stove. Hanne went below with her torch before anyone spoke. She found a crushed pin stub, a pivot that was true and seams that were dry. Tobi fitted a fresh pin in four minutes. They did it again at four knots, and Hanne went below again. Magnus watched the whole of it with his arms folded.

**Magnus**  
Good pin.
In his mouth it was a speech.

In the Sound that afternoon the swell ran two and a half metres from astern, and she went out carrying a hundred and forty people's weight in water ballast, the tanks gauged to the tonne, because Hanne would not certify a boat that had only ever been tried light. The boat lifted her stern on the first wave with the board down, and she did not swing. Adaeze stood at the rail with one hand flat on her chest and did not speak until the fifth wave had passed. Hanne did not call her in at five. She kept her on the heading for forty minutes, well over two hundred waves, and read the compass off her board, and wrote, and wrote again. Then she brought her back to the slip and went below with the torch before she would put her name to anything. The trunk lid was dry. The seams were dry. The pivot was true.

**Hanne**  
Eleven degrees at the worst, and that was the worst of forty minutes, not just of five waves. Not fifteen. Loaded to a hundred and forty, and the trunk and the pivot clean after it. And I've seen what the board does not do, Adaeze. She still wants the rudder, and she still wants a helmsman who is awake. Both of those are in the boat.
Hanne laid the register on the wheelhouse table and put her finger on the line that mattered.

**Hanne**  
A hundred and forty seats on my certificate. Three hundred and ten names on the register. Five of those are the Calloways, standing by. They have a radio, high ground and a rule. The coastguard desk calls the house every hour from tomorrow noon. If the call is missed, or the gauge on Skerrow quay reads above four point two metres, the cutter leaves harbour for the quay and asks them again at the door. It can work that quay safely up to five metres and not above, so four point two is when it goes, not when it is too late. The desk owns that decision, not me. That leaves three hundred and five to carry. Two full crossings and a short third, each a little under six hours round trip. The sea builds through the last day. If the third has to wait for a window, it waits, and the cutter takes its twenty-five, with room for the five besides.

scenes.title: Three Crossings
paragraphs: *Tolland Slip to Pellam Bank · the day before the surge, 06:30*

The boat went out at half past six with a hundred and forty aboard, a bench on either side of the trunk, and a name the islanders had already given her: the Both. The second crossing left at half past twelve into rising swell, with Hanne's pencil never far from the line that said three. The third left at twenty past six in the evening with twenty-five people and a dog, into two point nine, and Illuminara sat on the trunk bench beside Tobi and did nothing but breathe when the stern lifted.

At ten to nine the last passenger stepped onto the shingle at Pellam Bank, into the headlights of the buses. A driver counted heads aloud, three hundred and five, and got the same number twice. Hanne's certificate, folded in her coat, carried two yard names on a single line.
On the bow ramp the two masters had not gone to the buses.

**Adaeze**  
Another fifty millimetres on the board and she'd hold the Sound like a church.

**Magnus**  
Another fifty and she'd dig on the bank like a spade.

They were still at it when the rain began, standing on the ramp with the shingle going dark around them, and neither moved off it. Behind them Illuminara put her blistered hands in her pockets, thought nothing wise, and listened. Far up the hill a lamp burned in the Calloway window. On the hour Hanne's handset said, in Ruth's flat voice, *still here,* and Hanne ticked it on her list. The gauge on Skerrow quay read three point one. The rule had not been touched, and it would be called again at nine.

critic_line: They did not solve grief by agreeing about the sea; they built a boat in which each memory became a condition the other was willing to test.

shared_strengths: Humane, dialogue-driven problem-solving with a clever central idea (one number read in two units) and a warm collaborative resolution. Strong images and the 'what did the sea do first' refrain. Dense technical detail, conflict resolved smoothly and an open ending may cool some readers.

The urgent rescue, old grief, craft knowledge, and slowly repaired trust create a strong humane engine. Dialogue carries both character and engineering ideas unusually well, while Illuminara's humility adds warmth. Some readers may tire during the lengthy certification and trial procedures, but the crossings deliver satisfying suspense and a restrained, memorable ending.
shared_reservations: Seven-eighths of a foot is two hundred and sixty-seven millimetres. Seven-tenths is two hundred and thirteen. The Marigold had been built fifty-four millimetres too shallow, and she had rolled on her moorings
She read her conditions aloud before anyone touched the engine.

translation_sl.title: REŠILNI ČOLN, KI STA GA ZGRADILI DVE LADJEDELNICI
translation_sl.deck: Poplavni val bo prispel čez devet dni, obsojeni trajekt pa ne more izpluti. Dve ladjedelnici, ki si že trideset let nista delili navoza, vsaka pomni utopitev, ki bi jo ponovilo plovilo druge; Illuminara ju vpraša, kaj je morje storilo najprej.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v devetih dneh: prepir na produ, dan v vsaki ladjedelnici, tla s krednimi črtami, kjer se ena številka izkaže za dve in vsak mojster pove, kaj bi moral videti, noč držanja trupa pri miru, pogoji inšpektorice ter preizkus v dveh morjih, medtem ko se ena družina odloči ostati, in trije prevozi.

scenes.title: Prepir na produ
paragraphs: *Skerrow, navoz Tolland · devet dni pred poplavnim valom, 06:40*

Trajekt je ležal tam, kjer ga je pustila oseka, z oplato na eni strani odprto kakor pločevinka. Obvestilo inšpektorice na vratih krmilnice je bilo staro tri dni. Napoved je bila novejša: poplavni val čez devet dni, visoka voda ob 21:40 in morje, ki bo preplavilo pomol ter vdrlo v spodnjo vas. Na Skerrowu je živelo tristo deset ljudi. Rezalnik obalne straže bi lahko prepeljal štirideset ljudi, če bi morje dovolilo, morja pa ni hotel nihče obljubljati.

Illuminara je prišla z ribiško barko, termovko in beležnico. Občinski uradnik je prosil za roke, ki bi lahko držale trup pri miru med spajanjem. Nihče je ni prosil za načrt in začenjala je razumeti, zakaj.
Dva človeka sta prišla do navoza z nasprotnih koncev proda in nihče od njiju ni upočasnil.

**Magnus**  
V moji hali je trup iz pogodbe Orsay. Štiriindvajset metrov, raven kakor miza, na plitvino pa sede kakor roka v rokavico. Do poldneva ga lahko spravim na navoz.

**Adaeze**  
In v prvem morju od krme pri Soundu se prevrne. Raven trup se ne oprime vode. Moj brat se je tega naučil v času, ki ga potrebuješ, da to izrečeš. Tristo ljudi ne bom poslala na pladenj.

**Magnus**  
Tvoja globoka kobilica pa obtiči ob Pellam Banku in nima kam z nosom, nato jo razbije v priboj. Moj oče se je tega naučil. Poglej kamne.
Nihče ni pogledal kamnov. Gledala sta drug drugega, kakor ljudje gledajo zid, ki so ga pomagali zgraditi.

**Illuminara**  
Med spajanjem lahko držim trup vodoravno in nekaj časa prenašam obremenitev skozenj. Ne znam narisati kobilice in ne znam narisati plitvine. Imata oba prav glede plovila drugega?

**Adaeze**  
Da.

**Magnus**  
Da.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bi rada preživela dan v vsaki ladjedelnici. Ne zato, da bi izbrala med vama. Da bi me popravila.
Magnus se je prvi zasmejal, kratko in nejevoljno. To je bil prvi zvok, ki sta ga v tridesetih letih ustvarila skupaj, in nihče od njiju drugemu tega ni odpustil.

scenes.title: Risalnica
paragraphs: *Ladjedelnica Oyelaran, risalnica · devet dni pred poplavnim valom, 15:10*

Kredne črte so prekrivale tla risalnice, vsak odmik označen v Adaezejinih ulomkih čevlja. Sedemnajstletniku po imenu Tobi so naročili, naj obiskovalko nauči skobljati les za kobilico, in odločil se je, da bo temeljit.

**Tobi**  
Palec naprej. Ne, vi potiskate les. Skobelj potiska. Tako. Slišite? To je oblancek, ne iver.

Illuminara je že stala v številnih stvareh, ki so se podirale, in nikoli ni slišala tega zvoka. Hrast je dišal kakor zadržani dih. *Uči me fant z žagovino v obrveh,* je pomislila, *in srečnejša sem kakor ves teden.*
Adaeze je prišla po stopnicah z dvema skodelicama in ni sedla.

**Adaeze**  
Kehindejeva barka je bila ravna. Dobra barka, hitra. Ko se je vračala z morjem za krmo, je val dvignil krmo, premec se je zaril in za pol sekunde pod seboj ni imela ničesar, s čimer bi se oprijela vode. Nato se je obrnila bokom na valove in naslednji val jo je pokončal.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj je morje storilo najprej?

**Adaeze**  
Dvignilo je krmo. Vsi sprašujejo, kako velik je bil val. Vi ste prva, ki sprašuje, kaj je storil najprej.

Illuminara je v beležnico zapisala *krma se dvigne, brez oprijema, obrne se bokom na valove* in pod to *odprto morje, valovi od krme*. Adaeze jo je opazovala pri pisanju, kakor človek opazuje neznanca, ki rokuje z orodjem, ki ga je sam izdelal.

**Adaeze**  
Kobilica ni teorija. Je del čolna, ki si zapomni vodo.

scenes.title: Plitvina
paragraphs: *Ladjedelnica Fenn, rampa in prod · osem dni pred poplavnim valom, 07:20*

Šestnajstletni Wick ji je položil verigo v roke in prestavil njen prijem, še preden jih je sklenila. Vse na rampi Fenn je bilo izmerjeno po lastnem merilu ladjedelnice, v desetinah čevlja, s svinčnikom na oplati. Magnus je hodil po produ ob njej in pripovedoval kamnom namesto njej.

**Magnus**  
Očetova barka je imela dobro globoko kobilico. Odlična za Sound. Pri Harbour Tarnu ni bilo pomola, samo plitvina kakor Pellam. Pripeljal jo je, da bi jo nasedel, kobilica pa je zagrabila prod in jo v hipu ustavila, medtem ko je priboj še prihajal. Prevrnila se je štirideset jardov od suhih kamnov.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj je morje storilo najprej?
Pogledal jo je, kakor da je bila predrzna. Nato je odgovoril.

**Magnus**  
Kobilica se je ustavila. Najprej. Nato se je prevrnila.

Tisto noč je Illuminara na list rjavega papirja iz ladjedelnice zapisala oba odgovora drugega ob drugega. Adaezejin brat je umrl na odprtem morju, z valovi za krmo in brez česa, kar bi se oprijelo. Magnusov oče je umrl na plitvini, z morjem na boku in s prevelikim oprijemom. *Dve barki,* je pomislila. *Dve različni minuti iste plovbe.* Nihče dotlej ni od enega trupa zahteval, da preživi oboje.

scenes.title: Sedem v dveh jezikih
paragraphs: *Staro jadralno podstrešje · sedem dni pred poplavnim valom, 21:30*

Svetloba svetilke in mojstra na nasprotnih straneh. Tobi in Wick sta stala ob steni z izrazom vajencev, ki pričakujeta, da ju bodo poslali ven. Illuminara je na tla s kredo narisala dva stolpca in vsako številko pretvorila v milimetre. V enem: ODPRTO MORJE, VALOVI OD KRME. Potreben je oprijem vzdolž trupa. V drugem: PLITVINA. Potrebno je ravno dno brez vsega, kar bi se lahko zarilo.

Na mizi je ležal tretji list, rjav na pregibih, najden na dnu otoške skrinje z načrti. Marigold, edina barka, ki sta jo ladjedelnici kdaj narisali skupaj, pred tridesetimi leti. Njena kobilica je bila označena s sedem.

**Illuminara**  
Na tem listu so roke obeh. Kaj pomeni sedem?

**Adaeze**  
Sedem osmin čevlja.

**Magnus**  
Sedem desetin. To je sedem vedno pomenilo.

Sedem osmin čevlja je dvesto sedeminšestdeset milimetrov. Sedem desetin je dvesto trinajst. Marigold so zgradili štiriinpetdeset milimetrov preplitvo; v noči po splavitvi se je na privezu zibala, trideset let pa je vsaka ladjedelnica natanko vedela, kdo je kriv.
Nihče ni rekel oprosti. Adaeze je vzela kredo in ob sedmico napisala 267. Magnus jo je čez dolg trenutek vzel od nje in pod to zapisal 213; oba sta stala in gledala razliko.

**Illuminara**  
Oba načrta sta dobra. Eno številko sta brala v dveh jezikih.

**Magnus**  
Potem mi pokažite čoln, ki zmore oboje, in nehal bom govoriti, da ga ni mogoče zgraditi.

**Adaeze**  
Plošča skozi dno. Spuščena v Soundu, z valovi od krme, ji da nekaj, s čimer se oprime.

**Magnus**  
Luknja v dnu čolna. Približno tako je umrl moj oče.

**Adaeze**  
Luknja ostane, kjer je, pod vodno gladino. Spremeni se ohišje okoli nje, zvarjeno do krova, da se morje v ohišju dvigne do zunanje gladine in nič više. Pokrov je nad obremenjeno vodno črto.

**Magnus**  
Ohišje poči. Potem je to luknja s pokrovom.

**Adaeze**  
Potem ga napolnimo z vodo in opazujemo vso noč, preden se premakne. In poslušajte, kaj ta plošča je. Oprijem vzdolž trupa in nič drugega. Ne krmari in ni balast. Še vedno potrebuje krmilo, težo na pravem mestu in človeka za krmilom, ki pozna morje od krme.

**Magnus**  
Na plitvini pa je plošča spuščena in se ustavi v hipu, kakor se je on.

**Tobi**  
Dvignemo jo, preden pristane. Če zadene prod napol spuščena, se mora umakniti navzgor, ne zariti. Zatič, ki se prelomi. Vitel za dvig in ročica, kadar vitel odpove.
Nekaj časa ni nihče odgovoril vajencu. Adaeze je pogledala Magnusa. Magnus je pogledal Wicka, ki je pogledal v tla, nato pa z nekaj truda Tobija.

**Illuminara**  
Ne morem vama povedati, ali bo delovalo. Lahko vprašam, kaj bi moral vsak od vaju videti, preden sprejme roko drugega na svojem delu.

**Adaeze**  
V morju višine dva metra in pol od krme, s spuščeno ploščo, pet zaporednih valov obdrži smer znotraj petnajstih stopinj. Izmerjeno z inšpektoričinim kompasom, ne po spominu. Sicer Kehindejeva barka znova pluje z mojim imenom.

**Magnus**  
Ko se dotakne proda, pod njenim dnom ni ničesar. Plošča je z zatičem ali ročico spravljena v dvajsetih sekundah, jaz pa jo dvakrat opazujem pri nasedanju, enkrat počasi in enkrat ne. Sicer so pod tristo ljudmi očetova barka.
Nato sta oba storila tisto, na kar je drugi čakal trideset let, in napadla načrt namesto človeka.

**Magnus**  
Vaša plošča je narisana za globoki Sound. Sto petdeset milimetrov ji odvzamemo od globine, zatič pa se prelomi pri obremenitvi, pri kateri lahko opazujem prelom.

**Adaeze**  
Sto petdeset je oprijem, ki bi ga raje obdržala.

**Magnus**  
Potem se zarije.

**Adaeze**  
Vaša krma pa je odrezana naravnost. Morje od krme sede na ravno krmo kakor dlan na mizo. Hočem, da jo oblikujete, preden zaupam plošči, da jo bo držala.
Nekaj časa ni spregovoril nihče. Svetilka je tiktakala. Zunaj se je oseka umikala čez kamne.

**Adaeze**  
Potem bo plošča krajša. Vi pa prerežete svoj trup Orsay.

**Magnus**  
Trupa Orsay ni še nihče rezal. Sam ga bom prerezal v svoji hali, vi pa preverite moja rebra v svojih enotah.

**Adaeze**  
Jaz pa oblikujem krmo po vašem načrtu, v vaših desetinah.

Na rjavem listu je pod Tobijev zatič Adaeze zapisala Magnusov pogoj in se podpisala, Magnus pa je zapisal njenega in se podpisal; vsaka številka je bila v čevljih ali desetinah ter znova v milimetrih. Med pisanjem nihče ni pogledal navzgor.

**Magnus**  
Kdo je odgovoren za kaj?

**Adaeze**  
Plošča, ohišje in tečaj so moji. Trup, rampa in okvir okoli odprtine so vaši.

**Magnus**  
Obremenitev vašega tečaja preverim v vaših enotah.

**Adaeze**  
Jaz pa vaša rebra v vaših. Nato oba vse še enkrat preveriva v milimetrih in podpiševa liste drug drugega.

**Illuminara**  
Med rezanjem jo bom držala pri miru.

scenes.title: Mirovanje
paragraphs: *Navoz Tolland, hala dve · štiri dni pred poplavnim valom, 02:10*

Trije dnevi so šli v trup po vrstnem redu, ki ga je določil list Hanne Voss. Prvi dan je ladjedelnica Fenn odstranila krov in pripeljala trup Orsay na navoz. Drugi dan je Oyelaranova delavnica za pločevino zvila ohišje, ladjedelnici pa sta v izmeničnih izmenah izdelali okvir okoli črte odprtine, tako da nobena ni spala, medtem ko so bile roke druge na barki. Tretji dan je Hanne z baterijsko svetilko pregledala vsako rebro, zavrnila dva zvara in preostale odobrila opolnoči, nič prej. Šele nato so smeli prerezati dno.
Zdaj je stala na podstavkih, s črto svetilne svetlobe tam, kjer bo odprtina. Štirinajst ton oplate se je hotelo razpreti v trenutku, ko bo Tobijeva žaga končala prvi rez; ravni trup se grdo odpre.

Illuminara je obe dlani položila na oplato ob črti in prevzela obremenitev skozi sebe, po rokah in hrbtenici v navoz, kakor človek drži vrata proti vetru. Oplata je ostala ravna. Petdeset minut so Magnus, Tobi in Adaeze rezali in merili, ona pa se ni premaknila.

To jo je stalo. Roke so se ji tresle veliko prej, preden je bila odprtina končana, in ko je Magnus, ne da bi pogledal gor, rekel, da lahko spusti, je sedla na obrnjen škaf in ni mogla dvigniti skodelice. Tobi ji je prinesel čaj in z resnim obrazom še skobelj.

**Tobi**  
Vaš prijem je še vedno napačen.
*Dobro,* je pomislila in znova jo je presenetilo, kako močno je to mislila.

scenes.title: Dve morji
paragraphs: *Hrib na Skerrowu, Pellam Bank in Skerrow Sound · dva dni pred poplavnim valom, 06:00*

Družina Ruth Calloway ni prišla na navoz. Illuminara je namesto tega odšla na hrib in našla Ruth na pragu s termovko. V hiši jih je živelo pet, cerkev, kjer je ležala njena mati, pa je bila štiriintrideset metrov nad morjem.

**Ruth**  
Preživela sem enajst napovedi. Ostajamo.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj bi pomenilo, da je ostati manj podobno stavi?

**Ruth**  
Radio, ki deluje. In nekdo, ki pride po nas, če se motim.

**Illuminara**  
To bom odnesla inšpektorici. Če tega ne more zagotoviti, se bom vrnila in vam povedala.

Med rezom in vodo sta minila dva dneva. Ohišje so zvarili, napolnili do pokrova in opazovali vso noč; zdržalo je. Namestili so dvigalo in ročico. Na navozu se je Tobijev zatič v preizkusni napravi prelomil pri obremenitvi, ki jo je določil, in pri isti obremenitvi še drugič. Ob prvi svetlobi je zdrsnila po navozu, grda, z jaškom po sredini kakor hrbtenico.
Hanne Voss je imela šestdeset let in je zavrnila spričevala za veliko lepše barke. Preden se je kdo dotaknil motorja, je na glas prebrala svoje pogoje.

**Hanne**  
Najprej meje za prekinitev. Nagib preseže petnajst stopinj in ostane tam, odpokličem jo. Plošča se na ukaz ne odzove v dvajsetih sekundah, odpokličem jo. Voda doseže pokrov jaška, odpokličem jo. Značilna višina morja preseže tri metre, odpokličem jo. O tem se ne bom prepirala ne z eno ladjedelnico ne z drugo in tudi ne z vami.

Pred plitvino je pregledala celo barko in pustila obema mojstroma, da jo pri tem opazujeta. Z baterijsko svetilko je posvetila po jašku, z roko zdrsnila vzdolž šivov ohišja, preverila zračnost tečaja, odčitala prosti bok glede na balast ter sama preizkusila dvigalo in nato ročico, z uro v drugi roki. Sedemnajst sekund z ročico. Zapisala je.

Pri Pellam Banku je ob naraščajoči plimi barka s spravljeno ploščo zadela prod pri dveh vozlih. Njeno ravno dno se je povzpelo po plitvini in ustavilo brez trzaja. Nato je po Hannejinem ukazu poskusila znova pri dveh vozlih z napol spuščeno ploščo. Plošča je udarila, zatič se je prelomil in plošča se je zavihala v jašek kakor roka, umaknjena z vroče peči. Hanne je šla pod krov z baterijsko svetilko, še preden je kdo spregovoril. Našla je zmečkan ostanek zatiča, raven tečaj in suhe šive. Tobi je v štirih minutah vstavil nov zatič. Ponovili so pri štirih vozlih in Hanne je znova šla pod krov. Magnus je vse opazoval s prekrižanimi rokami.

**Magnus**  
Dober zatič.
V njegovih ustih je bil to govor.

Tistega popoldneva je v Soundu od krme prihajalo dva metra in pol visoko valovanje, ona pa je izplula z vodnim balastom v teži sto štiridesetih ljudi, rezervoarji izmerjeni na tono natančno, ker Hanne ni hotela potrditi barke, ki je bila preizkušena samo prazna. Na prvem valu je barka s spuščeno ploščo dvignila krmo in se ni obrnila. Adaeze je stala ob ograji z dlanjo plosko na prsih in ni spregovorila, dokler ni minil peti val. Hanne je ni odpoklicala pri petih. Štirideset minut jo je držala v smeri, precej več kot dvesto valov, smer odčitavala s kompasne plošče ter zapisovala in znova zapisovala. Nato jo je pripeljala nazaj na navoz in z baterijsko svetilko šla pod krov, preden je bila pripravljena kar koli podpisati. Pokrov jaška je bil suh. Šivi so bili suhi. Tečaj je bil raven.

**Hanne**  
Enajst stopinj v najslabšem trenutku, in to je bilo najslabše v štiridesetih minutah, ne samo v petih valovih. Ne petnajst. Obremenjena za sto štirideset ljudi, jašek in tečaj pa sta po tem čista. In videla sem tudi, česa plošča ne počne, Adaeze. Še vedno potrebuje krmilo in še vedno potrebuje budnega krmarja. Oboje je na barki.
Hanne je ladijski register položila na mizo v krmilnici in s prstom pokazala na pomembno vrstico.

**Hanne**  
Na mojem spričevalu je sto štirideset sedežev. V registru je tristo deset imen. Pet je Callowayevih, pripravljeni so ostati. Imajo radio, visoko ležečo hišo in pravilo. Od jutri opoldne jih dežurna služba obalne straže pokliče vsako uro. Če se ne oglasijo ali merilnik na pomolu Skerrow pokaže več kot štiri cela dve metra, rezalnik zapusti pristanišče, pride do pomola in jih znova vpraša na vratih. Pri tem pomolu lahko varno dela do petih metrov, ne več, zato gre pri štiri cela dve, ne šele, ko je prepozno. Za to odločitev je odgovorna dežurna služba, ne jaz. Ostane tristo pet ljudi za prevoz. Dva polna prevoza in kratek tretji, vsak krog malo manj kot šest ur. Morje se bo ves zadnji dan krepilo. Če bo tretji prevoz moral čakati na okno, bo čakal, rezalnik pa bo vzel petindvajset ljudi, poleg prostora za tistih pet.

scenes.title: Trije prevozi
paragraphs: *Navoz Tolland do Pellam Banka · dan pred poplavnim valom, 06:30*

Barka je odplula ob pol sedmih zjutraj s sto štiridesetimi ljudmi, klopjo na vsaki strani jaška in imenom, ki so ji ga otočani že dali: Both. Drugi prevoz je odšel ob pol enih v naraščajoče valovanje, Hannejin svinčnik pa se ni oddaljil od črte, na kateri je pisalo tri. Tretji je odšel ob dvajset čez šest zvečer s petindvajsetimi ljudmi in psom, v morje višine dve celi devet; Illuminara je sedela na klopi ob jašku poleg Tobija in ni počela drugega kakor dihala, ko se je dvignila krma.

Deset minut pred deveto je zadnji potnik stopil na prod pri Pellam Banku, v svetlobo avtobusnih žarometov. Voznik je na glas preštel ljudi, tristo pet, in enako število dobil dvakrat. Hannejino spričevalo, zloženo v njenem plašču, je nosilo imeni obeh ladjedelnic v eni vrstici.
Mojstra na premčni rampi nista odšla k avtobusom.

**Adaeze**  
Še petdeset milimetrov plošče in v Soundu bi držala kakor cerkev.

**Magnus**  
Še petdeset in na plitvini bi se zarila kakor lopata.

Še vedno sta se prerekala, ko je začelo deževati; stala sta na rampi, okoli njiju je prod temnel, nihče pa se ni umaknil. Za njima je Illuminara vtaknila ožuljene roke v žepe, ni pomislila ničesar modrega in poslušala. Visoko na hribu je v oknu Callowayevih gorela luč. Ob polni uri je Hannejin sprejemnik z Ruthinim ravnim glasom povedal *še smo tukaj* in Hanne je to označila na seznamu. Merilnik na pomolu Skerrow je kazal tri cele ena. Pravilo še ni bilo sproženo in znova ga bodo preverili ob devetih.

translation_sl.critic_line: Žalosti nista razrešila tako, da bi se strinjala o morju; zgradila sta čoln, v katerem je vsak spomin postal pogoj, ki ga je bil drugi pripravljen preizkusiti.
